participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the deferred sentence order. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a copy of the deferred sentence order. It gives you the case number and the deferral period, and you will need it again at the DOJ stage.

Check your answer to "Was your sentence DEFERRED, rather than suspended? These are different and this route only works for a deferred imposition. Your sentencing order should say which." against Copy of the deferred sentence order, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Confirmation from the court record that no petition to revoke was filed. Ask the clerk to confirm from the case file whether a petition to revoke was ever filed during the deferral period. On a felony this is dispositive: § 46-18-204(1)(a) makes dismissal mandatory only where no revocation petition was filed. LegalEase will not assert this for you.

Check your answer to "Did the prosecuting agency ever file a petition to revoke your deferred sentence? If you are not sure, the clerk of court can tell you, and on a felony this is the fact that decides whether the court must grant your motion." against Confirmation from the court record that no petition to revoke was filed, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Obtain Copy of the dismissal order once granted. After the court signs the order, ask the clerk for a copy. It is enclosed with the CRISS request together with the deferred sentence order.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Obtained after the order issues, for the DOJ stage.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Documentation of compliance with the deferral conditions. Where the court asks for proof that you completed the conditions, obtain the discharge or payment records that show it.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The supervising probation office, the treatment provider, or the clerk's payment records
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Obtain only where the court or the prosecuting office questions completion.

participantActionRequired.description: Mail or hand delivery of the file-stamped motion to the county attorney's or city attorney's office that prosecuted the case, after filing.

File the motion, certificate of service and proposed order with the clerk of the court that issued the deferred sentence, in the EXISTING criminal case and under the same case number. This is a motion, not a new civil action. Contacting the clerk first is a required step in this track, not optional, because the published guidance acknowledges that some courts have their own procedures or provide different forms and that the case may already have been dismissed and sealed. Unit 2 is a separate mailed submission to DOJ CRISS.

entries: Motion in the sentencing court to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge and seal the case (custom_pleading)

A motion to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge and seal the case, with a certificate of service and a proposed order, filed in the court that issued the deferred sentence, under the SAME case number as the original criminal case.

A motion to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge and seal the case, with a certificate of service and a proposed order, filed in the court that issued the deferred sentence, under the SAME case number as the original criminal case.

A motion to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge and seal the case, with a certificate of service and a proposed order, filed in the court that issued the deferred sentence, under the SAME case number as the original criminal case.

The prayer asks the court to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge, seal the case, classify all records and data as confidential criminal justice information accessible to the public only by district court order upon good cause shown, and send a copy of the order to the prosecuting agency, and recites that the defendant will be responsible for providing a copy to the Department of Justice.
This is a motion in the existing criminal case rather than a new civil action, which is why no new filing fee is ordinarily expected.
